evidence.field: 后: graphic history; Shuowen; Guangyun; Middle Chinese categories
evidence.text: The entry reports 后 first in late Spring and Autumn bronze inscriptions, with the sense ‘ruler’, citing a bronze inscription for a ruler. It describes bronze forms oriented right as 后 and left as 司, while oracle forms show no directional distinction; it attributes the same-graph interpretation to Tang Lan and Li Xiaoding. Separately, it reports Wang Guowei’s identification of an oracle form written with 毓. It reproduces Shuowen’s account of 后 as a successor ruler represented as a person issuing commands, analyzed with 一 and 口, and lists Guangyun fanqie 胡口 and 胡遘, with Middle Chinese 匣母, 侯韻, upper and departing tones. These are competing historical accounts; they do not settle the graph’s decomposition or a sequence into received 后.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：后

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: A00511 后: Shuowen; senses; received-text citations
evidence.text: The entry gives Mandarin hòu and reproduces the Great Xu and Duan annotations of Shuowen: 后 as a successor ruler, represented as a person, with 一 and 口 in the analysis. It separately lists ‘king’, ‘feudal lord’, ‘ruler’s principal wife’, ‘earth deity’, and surname, with received-text citations including Shijing 商頌·玄鳥, Zuozhuan 僖公三十二年, Shujing 舜典, Guangyun 皇后也, and Han shu 景帝紀. Those citations attest lexicographic examples of distinct uses but do not date transitions among the senses or establish a childbirth-to-succession chain.
evidence.title: [A00511] 后 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: A01287-012 后 (後): textual substitution and standardization history
evidence.text: The entry says 后 and 後 were originally unrelated graphs but homophonous, and cites received-text substitution of 后 for 後 in Yili 大射 and Liji 大學. It also reports 后 for 後 in Song–Yuan and later popular literature. It states that mainland simplified-character tables promulgated in 1964 and 1986 used 后 as the simplified form of 後. This supports a whole-graph spelling loan and later standardization, distinct from a phonetic component inside 后; the entry does not identify the earliest loan occurrence or establish the ancient sound match independently of its homophony claim.
evidence.title: [A01287] 後 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.field: 後: proposed components, alternative phonetic analysis, cited early uses and Shuowen
evidence.text: The database proposes oracle 幺 + 夂 as an early graph for 後, analyzing 夂 as a foot and 幺 as a restraining cord, with 彳 added later. It records an alternative that 幺 is phonetic, attributed to Liu Zhao and He Linyi. It cites an oracle usage in 屯南2358 for succession/order, bronze examples for lagging, temporal ‘after’, descendants and an asserted ‘end’ sense, and Warring States bamboo examples for descendants/successor. It also reproduces Shuowen’s 遲也 analysis from 彳、幺、夊 and its separate ancient form 𨒥 from 辵. These are the database’s reports and interpretations; the cited artifacts/texts were not independently checked against primary editions here.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：後

evidence.field: Shuowen data search for 幺 and 後
evidence.text: The database’s Shuowen search reproduces 後 as ‘遲也’ and analyzes it from 彳、幺、夊, with the ancient form 𨒥 from 辵. Its same results identify 幺 separately as a graph meaning ‘small’ and shaped like a newly born child. This records the Shuowen tradition, not proof that 幺’s semantic or phonetic role in 後 is settled.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 說文資料搜索

search_audit.outcome: Inspected CUHK’s 後 entry and Shuowen search record, confirming its proposed component account, explicit alternative phonetic analysis of 幺, and cited early textual/inscription senses. Search did not verify pixel content or metadata for 后-seal. Unicode search found an official report mentioning U+540E but not the required character-specific kMandarin records.

gaps: The early graphic origin of 后 remains unsettled. CUHK reports the 后/司 same-graph or orientation account and separately reports Wang Guowei’s oracle 毓 identification; neither establishes a complete graphic sequence into received 后. No secure childbirth or rear-body depiction, component decomposition, or corruption path is demonstrated by the inspected sources.

CUHK reports late Spring and Autumn bronze attestation for 后 as ‘ruler’, but primary inscription editions were not independently inspected and possible earlier oracle forms are not securely dated or identified here.

The Ministry dictionary’s received-text examples document ruler, feudal-lord, and ruler’s-wife senses, but do not date transitions among them or establish the dossier’s proposed childbirth-to-succession semantic chain.

The Ministry dictionary supports classical spelling use of 后 for 後 and names Yili and Liji examples, plus 1964/1986 standardization. It does not establish the first loan date or independently establish the ancient sound match.

The 後 account of 幺 + 夂 as cord plus foot competes with the explicit proposal that 幺 is phonetic. No same-system reconstructed pronunciation comparison for 幺 was retrieved, so its role cannot be tested here.
No source establishing the original object/name/pronunciation of an alleged depicted tool or weapon was found; the inspected evidence does not support such an analysis for 后.
Exact Unicode Unihan records for 后, 後 and 口 failed to open. The supplied local kMandarin rows remain local metadata only; official upstream character-specific readings were not verified.

The supplied Baxter–Sagart local rows were checked, including distinct OC notation for 后 and 後 and the differing 口 reading, but the upstream reconstruction PDF failed to open. The local file rows are not emitted as independently verified external evidence.

The Commons page for 后-seal.svg and its imageinfo API were inaccessible; the exact image and purported public-domain metadata could not be verified. The Shuowen Radical 335 page is verified as a modern seal-style redrawing with CC BY-SA 3.0 licensing, but its SVG fetch failed and pixels were not inspected; it is not an early inscription specimen.

No image selected: the accessible modern redraw may illustrate a received Shuowen seal-style form, but pixels were inaccessible and it does not resolve early graphic history. No broad dictionary-content reuse permission was found, so no tracked extract is recommended.
